cards.front: What are tú (affirmative) commands and how are they formed?
cards.back:
Tú affirmative commands tell someone (informally) to do something. For most -ar verbs, drop the -as from tú form:
  bailas → ¡Baila! (Dance!)
For most -er/-ir verbs, drop the -es/-es:
  bebes → ¡Bebe! (Drink!)
cards.grammarNote: The tú affirmative command of regular verbs = 3rd person singular present tense form (él/ella form).

cards.front: Irregular tú commands — the 'Go Vino Sal Pod Ten Ven Di Haz' group
cards.back:
ir → ve (go)
poner → pon (put/play)
salir → sal (go out)
poder → n/a (not used as command)
tener → ten (have)
venir → ven (come)
decir → di (say/tell)
hacer → haz (do/make)
cards.grammarNote: Memorize these — they do NOT follow the regular pattern. Common in daily conversation.
Baila is the tú command of bailar. Conmigo = with me. This is playful and direct — perfect on the dance floor.
Dame = da (tú command of dar) + me (indirect object pronoun, attached). Object pronouns attach to affirmative commands.
Ven is the irregular tú command of venir (to come). Conmigo = with me.
Dime = di (irregular command of decir) + me (attached pronoun). Nombre = name.
Mira is the tú command of mirar (to look/watch). A regular -ar verb: ella mira → ¡mira!
Escucha is the tú command of escuchar (to listen). Regular -ar verb. Canción (song) is feminine — esta canción.
Bebe is the tú command of beber (to drink) — regular -er verb: él bebe → ¡bebe! Salud = cheers.
Sal is the irregular tú command of salir (to go out). Con nosotros = with us.
Ponme = pon (irregular command of poner) + me (for me, attached). Otra vez = again.

cards.front: How do you form NEGATIVE tú commands?
cards.back:
Use the present subjunctive (tú form) with no:
  no bailes (don't dance)
  no te vayas (don't go/leave)
  no me digas (don't tell me)
Object pronouns go BEFORE the verb in negative commands.
cards.grammarNote: Negative tú commands are very different from affirmative ones — they use the subjunctive, not the tú present.

cards.front: Don't go! The night is just getting started.
cards.back: ¡No te vayas! La noche apenas está empezando.
cards.grammarNote: No te vayas — the subjunctive of irse (to leave/go). Te is placed before vayas in a negative command. Apenas = just/barely.

cards.front: Where do object pronouns go in affirmative vs. negative commands?
cards.back:
AFFIRMATIVE — pronoun ATTACHES to the end of the command:
  Dime (tell me), dame (give me), llámame (call me)
NEGATIVE — pronoun goes BEFORE the verb:
  no me digas (don't tell me), no me des (don't give me)
cards.grammarNote: When attaching a pronoun makes a word 3+ syllables, a written accent may be needed to preserve the original stress: llama → llámame.

cards.front: Turn these into tú commands: (to dance), (to come), (to give + me), (to listen)
cards.grammarNote: Regular -ar verbs use the él/ella present tense form. Venir is irregular (ven). Dame attaches the pronoun directly to the command.
